thesis: TG Therapeutics reported Q3 2026 before the Nov 9 open (8-K). Total revenue was about $259.9M, BRIUMVI U.S. net product revenue grew about 52% to $232.6M, and the company raised its full-year BRIUMVI U.S. target to about $915-920M, with total 2026 revenue expected to exceed $1B. The shares rose about 5.9% to $63.38 on 2.9x volume, within 0.4% of the 52-week high. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: EPS came in below consensus (about $0.35 vs $0.43), and pivotal Phase 3 subcutaneous BRIUMVI results are expected around year-end or early 2027, a pending binary event. Litigation and governance checks found only a July 2026 plaintiff-firm solicitation about possible self-dealing and older 2016/2022 securities cases, with no scheduled ruling or restatement. A confirmed, company-specific raise with an open earnings-miss and pending-readout counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: BRIUMVI growth slows below the raised guide or the subcutaneous Phase 3 disappoints, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$59.83).

thesis: Surgery Partners is being taken private. Its buyer, a Bon Secours Mercy Health affiliate (HealthSpan Partners), raised its cash offer on Nov 9 to $25 a share from $23.50, after an unsolicited, non-binding $28-a-share proposal from a third party on Nov 3; holders may also receive up to $1.61 a share in ticking fees if closing slips past March 1, 2027. The shares rose about 14.0% to $26.46 on 3.0x volume, above the amended cash price, so the stock now trades on deal mechanics and the chance of a higher bid rather than on operating fundamentals. A plaintiff firm is investigating the going-private terms, and a March 2026 plaintiff-firm securities investigation and a Texas physician-poaching suit were found, with no scheduled ruling. A deal-bound, arbitrage-driven price makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: A definitive higher bid is signed, or the deal breaks and the shares re-rate on fundamentals.
sources: Investing.com / Reuters (bid raised to $25 after $28 rival proposal): https://investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bon-secours-affiliate-sweetens-bid-for-surgery-partners-to-up-to-6-billion-5012485

thesis: Fervo Energy rose about 26.3% to $11.40 on 2.7x volume after its Nov 9 Q3 report, which said its first GeoBlock at Cape Station reached commercial operation on Sept 30, ahead of schedule; the loss of $0.07 a share was narrower than expected, while revenue of about $116K missed. The stock remains far below its $27 May IPO price and $42.65 high. Hagens Berman is investigating whether the IPO documents disclosed transmission-curtailment risk and the issues raised in an Oct 6 Morpheus Research short report (thermal decline, water loss, seismicity-related damage); no case has been filed and this run found no company rebuttal. An operating milestone set against unresolved short-report allegations about the core resource leaves the evidence unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Cape Station output data refute the short-report allegations and revenue scales as plants come online.

thesis: LifeStance reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5 (8-K): revenue grew 25% to $455.9M, adjusted EBITDA grew 70% to $68.4M, net income was $22.4M, and full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance was raised. On Nov 9 the shares rose about 6.0% to $14.60 on 8.5x volume after Canaccord raised its target, and this run also found a priced secondary offering of 45M shares at $13.12 by selling stockholders (no proceeds to the company), expected to close Nov 12. That share offering meets the dilution_risk criterion as written, even though it adds supply rather than new shares. Litigation checks found a 2026 data-privacy settlement and older 2021-2022 plaintiff-firm investigations, with no scheduled ruling or restatement. A real beat-and-raise with a risk flag present makes this low under the rubric.
invalidation: Clinician and visit growth slow or the raised guide is cut, or sustained trading below the $13.12 offering price.

thesis: TIC Solutions rose about 9.0% to $11.30 on 4.8x volume, continuing its reaction to the Nov 5 Q3 report: revenue of $639.6M beat estimates, organic growth was about 8.4%, adjusted EPS was $0.18, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $2.24-2.27B. The open counter-case is cash and leverage: cash fell to $197.9M from $439.5M at year-end, and nine-month operating cash flow was only $36.6M. The governance check found that predecessor Acuren Corp filed an 8-K with Item 4.02 (non-reliance on previously issued financial statements) on Mar 27, 2025, restating 2024 interim statements for an income-tax error, which is within 3 years and meets the governance_history criterion. A risk flag present makes this low.
invalidation: Cash generation improves and leverage falls while organic growth holds, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$10.70).
sources: Finviz (Q3 results, raised revenue view, cash and leverage): https://finviz.com/news/417279/tic-solutions-misses-eps-by-a-penny-but-an-organic-growth-inflection-and-raised-revenue-outlook-shift-the-debate-to-cash-and-leverage

thesis: James Hardie rose about 7.3% to $29.89 on 4.3x volume after it was named to join the S&P MidCap 400, replacing Roku, effective Nov 11; one analyst estimated about 79M shares of passive buying. That is mechanical index demand. The underlying Nov 5 fiscal Q2 2027 report beat on sales (+24%) and margin and reaffirmed the full-year outlook, but the shares fell about 7.9% after hours on a weaker second-half outlook and cost pressure at the high end of its range. Litigation checks found an Australian class action over 2025 disclosures (served June 2026) and U.S. plaintiff-firm investigations tied to the AZEK merger, with no scheduled ruling found. An index-driven move on top of a weaker forward outlook makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: Second-half results beat the softened outlook and housing demand recovers.

thesis: Immunovant rose about 15.2% to $35.18 on 2.8x volume after Nov 9 Phase 2 results for IMVT-1402 in difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: the 600 mg dose met the primary endpoint (92.5% vs 75.6% maintaining ACR20 at Week 28), but the 300 mg dose showed no difference from placebo (p=0.94), and the company said further development in Sjogren's disease beyond the ongoing trial is unlikely. Litigation checks found only plaintiff-firm fiduciary-duty solicitations, with no filed case or restatement. A high-dose win offset by a failed low dose and a narrowed pipeline leaves the evidence mixed, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Larger trials confirm the high-dose effect and the company sets a clear registrational path.

thesis: Vir rose about 11.9% to $13.66 on 3.9x volume after Nov 9 Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 results in chronic hepatitis delta, presented at AASLD: the elebsiran plus tobevibart combination met the primary endpoint (44% undetectable virus with normalized ALT at Week 48 vs 0%) and the key secondary endpoint (79% undetectable virus vs 0%). The Nov 4 Q3 report (8-K) showed about $901M of cash and investments before $90M of Gilead upfront payments, with runway guided into 2H 2028. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: Gilead's Hepcludex was approved for this indication in May and Mirum reported a Phase 3 win in September, the trial was small (124 patients), and a U.S. filing around mid-2027 depends on ECLIPSE 2 and 3 data due in Q1 2027. Litigation checks found no lawsuit or restatement; the CFO left in August to pursue another opportunity and the CMO stepped down in April, neither tied to problems. A confirmed, company-specific Phase 3 win with an open competitive and data-maturity counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: ECLIPSE 2 or 3 data disappoint or regulators require more, or a close back below the pre-data level (~$12.21).
sources: Fierce Biotech (Phase 3 hepatitis delta win, competition): https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/virs-phase-3-hepatitis-delta-win-fuels-push-eclipse-gilead

thesis: Dropbox fell about 6.0% to $32.59 on 3.5x volume, and this run found no company disclosure or new analyst action explaining it. The Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K) showed revenue up only 0.5% to $637.3M with a 42.2% non-GAAP operating margin, a small full-year revenue raise, a planned $350M Tigris Data acquisition, and an approximately 9% workforce reduction announced Oct 28. Litigation checks found a pending reconsideration decision in the Entangled Media patent case (hearing held Nov 2), a Delaware challenge to the Nevada reincorporation in motion-to-dismiss briefing, and a data-breach class action, none meeting a risk_flags criterion. Near-zero growth and an unexplained heavy-volume decline leave the read unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Revenue growth re-accelerates on the AI products and the Tigris deal, with margins held.

thesis: Warby Parker reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5: revenue grew 10.4% to $244.7M, average revenue per customer rose 6.7%, adjusted EBITDA was $28.6M with net income of $5.6M, and it guided Q4 revenue to $243-253M (+15-20%) while narrowing full-year revenue to $966-976M. The shares jumped about 22.5% that day and another 18.5% to $30.20 on Nov 9 on 3.3x volume, a new 52-week high, with coverage citing an analyst upgrade. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: free cash flow was negative (-$2.0M) on Intelligent Eyewear launch spending, the full-year range was narrowed rather than raised, and the launch itself (pre-orders from Nov 12) is still unproven. Litigation checks found only a settled wage-and-hour case (final accounting hearing Dec 2) and routine matters, with no restatement. A confirmed, company-specific beat with an open launch-execution counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: Q4 revenue lands below the 15-20% growth guide or Intelligent Eyewear demand disappoints, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$21.29).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). Roivant reported fiscal Q2 on Nov 9 (8-K): LISRAYA (brepocitinib), approved by the FDA in August, generated $31.0M of net product revenue in its first five weeks; total revenue was $35.1M; the net loss attributable to Roivant widened to $191.6M; and cash and securities were $4.2B. The shares rose about 4.6% to $40.66, above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: CLARITY-1 and CLARITY-2 met their endpoints in non-infectious uveitis, but the sNDA is not expected until 1H calendar 2027, so that indication is not yet approved. An Investor Day is set for Dec 9. This run found no lawsuit with a scheduled ruling. A confirmed launch with the uveitis approval still pending keeps this at medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, or FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene eased about 1.6% to $68.59, just above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run found no company disclosure dated today. Recent items: the CFO plans to step down in December under a named succession, with the company backing its guidance (routine succession); it is suing HHS/CMS over 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings it says will cost $448M; and it is exiting Hawaii's QUEST Medicaid program on Dec 31. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58 against a $0.07 consensus. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
sources: Becker's Payer (star-ratings suit, Hawaii exit): https://www.beckerspayer.com/?p=30233

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). NWL rose about 7.6% to $5.89, slightly above the $5.82 cost, and this run's search found no new company disclosure. It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance, against 3.7% sales growth and a 90bp normalized margin gain. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 4 trading days ago), and there is no new fact, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
sources: Investing.com (NWL quote page, no new items): https://uk.investing.com/equities/newell-rubber

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 9 on the Nov 6 proposal). JFrog rose about 7.2% to $108.22, a new 52-week high, and this run's search found no new company disclosure dated today. The thesis rests on the Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 31% to $179.2M, cloud revenue grew 60%, net dollar retention rose to 124%, the non-GAAP operating margin was 22.7%, and free cash flow was $66.5M. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: GAAP operating income is still slightly negative, share-based compensation was $41.8M in the quarter, the Q4 revenue guide implies only about 2-3% sequential growth, and the size of any full-year raise against prior guidance remains unconfirmed. The early-exit guard applies (opened today). This stays medium.
invalidation: Cloud growth or net dollar retention decelerates materially, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$74.62).
